title: Single-shot hyperspectral wavefront imaging
core_idea: A hyperspectral wavefront sensing scheme that replaces the conventional Hartmann mask with a multicore fiber: it leverages the angular memory effect and the limited spectral correlation width of the fiber to encode wavefront gradients as spot displacements and spectral information as uncorrelated speckle patterns, enabling compact, single-shot retrieval of spatial and spectral wavefront information with a tunable spatial–spectral resolution trade-off.
tldr: Use a multicore-fiber Hartmann-like mask and speckle-spectral encoding (via angular memory effect and spectral decorrelation) to perform compact, single-shot hyperspectral wavefront measurements for applications such as spatio-spectral metrology, adaptive optics, and dispersive imaging.
